ELUCIDATION OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF BARITO KUALA REGENCY
NUMBER 4 OF 2015
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL
The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb and damage psychological (psychic), physical, sexual and economic security. This is philosophically stated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire Nation and the Homeland of Indonesia.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), and is thus obligated to fulfill these provisions.

Human Rights state that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government. Through Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation.

Protection is necessary to prevent violence and physical, mental and sexual exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, and education that is appropriate to their physical and psychological development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents are obligated to understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and legal apparatus that defend the interests of children is necessary for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled on defending the best interests of the child (the best interest of the child) is necessary to realize protection that is legal in nature.

The Government of Barito Kuala Regency has established an Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) as a center for empowerment of women victims of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

From the above framework, the Government of Barito Kuala Regency is responsible for taking legal actions to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children, with the creation of the Regional Regulation of Barito Kuala Regency concerning Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence.

Article 5
Letter a Sufficiently clear Letter b The basic rights referred to include the right to education and access to parents during the handling process.
Letter c What is meant by the right to equal protection is related to status, citizenship, race, skin color, gender, language, belief, religion, politics or other opinions, ethnicity or social life, property, disability, birth or other status.
Letter d Sufficiently clear Letter e What is meant by the right to obtain freedom is the freedom to express one's views on all matters, including those related to legal processes, care and temporary protection as well as identification and implementation of subsequent solutions.

Article 3
Letter a What is meant by trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by means of the threat of force, use of force, abduction, confinement, forgery of documents or identity, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over that person or another person, whether carried out within the country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
Letter b What is meant by exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim which includes prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical sexual reproductive organs or unlawfully, transferring/utilizing power or transplanting organs and or body tissues or utilizing the power or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
Letter c Sufficiently clear Letter d What is meant by witness is a person who sees, hears and experiences events of violence and human rights violations.
Letter e Mediation is carried out for cases of domestic violence that fall into the category of complaint offenses as regulated in Law No. 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence.

Article 9
The obligations of family and/or parents as referred to in Article 6 letter c and letter d, who legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence and protect women and children as family members.

Article 12
Paragraph (1) Letter a What is meant by complaint services is a series of actions carried out by the organizer of integrated service institutions to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families and/or the community.
Letter b What is meant by health services is efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
Letter c What is meant by legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants or advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive.
Letter d What is meant by repatriation is returning women and children victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
Letter e What is meant by social rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
What is meant by social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
Letter f What is meant by accompaniment services is that victims have the right to be accompanied by social workers at the investigation, prosecution or examination level.
Paragraph (2) What is meant by minimum service standards is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal aid, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence.
Paragraph (3) Sufficiently clear

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the Regency of Bupati Barito Kuala.
2. Regional Government is the Regent together with regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration of Barito Kuala Regency.
3. Family Planning, Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Agency, abbreviated as BKBP3A is the Regional Work Unit of Barito Kuala Regency.
4. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively through information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral.
5. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Human Trafficking Crimes, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts of human trafficking crimes in Barito Kuala Regency.
6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those in the womb.
8. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, class, social status, socio-economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
9. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim;
10. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions. Coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life;
11. Violence against children is any action that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom.
12. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household;
13. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited;
14. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death.
15. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
16. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing a proper livelihood, care or maintenance.
17. Psychological violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
18. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
19. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Police, Prosecutor's Office, Courts, Social Institutions, or other parties who know or hear or violence against women has occurred.
20. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
21. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
22. Optimal service is a dynamic effort consisting of various interrelated parts, followed by performance offered by one party to another party by providing benefits, in order to achieve the best goal.
23. Information is a message (speech or expression) or collection of messages consisting of order sequences of symbols, or meanings that can be interpreted from messages or collections of messages and can be recorded or transmitted.
24. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and or mother;
25. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children and among people who are their dependents.
26. Society is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 12
Paragraph (1) Letter a What is meant by complaint services is a series of actions carried out by the organizer of integrated service institutions to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families and/or the community.
Letter b What is meant by health services is efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
Letter c What is meant by legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants or advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive.
Letter d What is meant by repatriation is returning women and children victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
Letter e What is meant by social rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
What is meant by social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
Letter f What is meant by accompaniment services is that victims have the right to be accompanied by social workers at the investigation, prosecution or examination level.
Paragraph (2) What is meant by minimum service standards is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal aid, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence.
Paragraph (3) Sufficiently clear

Article 21
(1) Regional governments establish partnerships with the business sector in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.
(2) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) are conducted through: a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of acts of violence;
b. education and training for women victims of acts of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of acts of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
d. fostering and increasing economic independence of women victims of acts of violence.
(3) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), are set forth in the form of an agreement.

ELUCIDATION OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF BARITO KUALA REGENCY
NUMBER 4 OF 2015
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL
The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb and damage psychological (psychic), physical, sexual and economic security. This is philosophically stated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire Nation and the Homeland of Indonesia.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), and is thus obligated to fulfill these provisions.

Human Rights state that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government. Through Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation.

Protection is necessary to prevent violence and physical, mental and sexual exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, and education that is appropriate to their physical and psychological development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents are obligated to understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and legal apparatus that defend the interests of children is necessary for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled on defending the best interests of the child (the best interest of the child) is necessary to realize protection that is legal in nature.

The Government of Barito Kuala Regency has established an Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) as a center for empowerment of women victims of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

From the above framework, the Government of Barito Kuala Regency is responsible for taking legal actions to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children, with the creation of the Regional Regulation of Barito Kuala Regency concerning Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the Regency of Bupati Barito Kuala.
2. Regional Government is the Regent together with regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration of Barito Kuala Regency.
3. Family Planning, Women's Empowerment and Child Protection Agency, abbreviated as BKBP3A is the Regional Work Unit of Barito Kuala Regency.
4. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively through information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral.
5. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Human Trafficking Crimes, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts of human trafficking crimes in Barito Kuala Regency.
6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those in the womb.
8. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, class, social status, socio-economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
9. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim;
10. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions. Coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life;
11. Violence against children is any action that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom.
12. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household;
13. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited;
14. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death.
15. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
16. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing a proper livelihood, care or maintenance.
17. Psychological violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
18. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
19. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Police, Prosecutor's Office, Courts, Social Institutions, or other parties who know or hear or violence against women has occurred.
20. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
21. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
22. Optimal service is a dynamic effort consisting of various interrelated parts, followed by performance offered by one party to another party by providing benefits, in order to achieve the best goal.
23. Information is a message (speech or expression) or collection of messages consisting of order sequences of symbols, or meanings that can be interpreted from messages or collections of messages and can be recorded or transmitted.
24. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and or mother;
25. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children and among people who are their dependents.
26. Society is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 8
(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 6 letter b, shall be implemented in the form of community participation.
(2) The form of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children; b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
c. participating in providing assistance and/or handling of victims of acts of violence.
(3) The form of community participation as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be implemented responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 12
Paragraph (1) Letter a What is meant by complaint services is a series of actions carried out by the organizer of integrated service institutions to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children submitted by victims, families and/or the community.
Letter b What is meant by health services is efforts that include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
Letter c What is meant by legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants or advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive.
Letter d What is meant by repatriation is returning women and children victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
Letter e What is meant by social rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
What is meant by social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
Letter f What is meant by accompaniment services is that victims have the right to be accompanied by social workers at the investigation, prosecution or examination level.
Paragraph (2) What is meant by minimum service standards is a performance benchmark for integrated service units in providing complaint handling services, health services, social rehabilitation, law enforcement and legal aid, as well as repatriation and social reintegration for women and children victims of violence.
Paragraph (3) Sufficiently clear

Article 2
Letter a The principle of humanity serves as the foundation for the concept of protection of women and children from acts of violence, constituting respect for human rights and the dignity and worth of every citizen and resident of Indonesia proportionally (the second principle of Pancasila) Letter b The principle of justice and gender equality that gender justice is a process to be fair to men and women. Gender equality is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social, cultural, and governmental activities and equality in enjoying the results of development.
Letter c The principle of protection is a principle that functions to provide protection to women and children in order to provide tranquility in family and community life.
Letter d The principle of the best interests of women and children, that all actions concerning women and children carried out by families, communities, and Regional Governments are to fulfill the rights of women and children as regulated in laws and regulations.
Letter e The principle of non-discrimination, that in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence there shall be no differentiation on the basis of age, sex, race, ethnicity, tribe, religion and between groups.

I. GENERAL
The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb and damage psychological (psychic), physical, sexual and economic security. This is philosophically stated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire Nation and the Homeland of Indonesia.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), and is thus obligated to fulfill these provisions.

Human Rights state that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government. Through Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation.

Protection is necessary to prevent violence and physical, mental and sexual exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, and education that is appropriate to their physical and psychological development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents are obligated to understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and legal apparatus that defend the interests of children is necessary for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled on defending the best interests of the child (the best interest of the child) is necessary to realize protection that is legal in nature.

The Government of Barito Kuala Regency has established an Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) as a center for empowerment of women victims of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

From the above framework, the Government of Barito Kuala Regency is responsible for taking legal actions to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children, with the creation of the Regional Regulation of Barito Kuala Regency concerning Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence.

CHAPTER VIII
COOPERATION AND PARTNERSHIP
Part One
Cooperation

Article 24
The community may conduct supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children from acts of violence organized by the regional government through a mechanism of conveying aspirations to the Regent or to the DPRD.

Article 21
(1) Regional governments establish partnerships with the business sector in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.
(2) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) are conducted through: a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of acts of violence;
b. education and training for women victims of acts of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of acts of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
d. fostering and increasing economic independence of women victims of acts of violence.
(3) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), are set forth in the form of an agreement.

Article 22
Paragraph (1) what is meant by guidance on the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children from acts of violence is efforts undertaken by regional government and society to realize the achievement of the objectives of prevention and protection of women and children from acts of violence.

Paragraph (2) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (3) Sufficiently clear

REGIONAL REGULATION OF BARITO KUALA REGENCY
NUMBER 4 OF 2015
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL
The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb and damage psychological (psychic), physical, sexual and economic security. This is philosophically stated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire Nation and the Homeland of Indonesia.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), and is thus obligated to fulfill these provisions.

Human Rights state that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government. Through Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation.

Protection is necessary to prevent violence and physical, mental and sexual exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, and education that is appropriate to their physical and psychological development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents are obligated to understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and legal apparatus that defend the interests of children is necessary for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled on defending the best interests of the child (the best interest of the child) is necessary to realize protection that is legal in nature.

The Government of Barito Kuala Regency has established an Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) as a center for empowerment of women victims of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

From the above framework, the Government of Barito Kuala Regency is responsible for taking legal actions to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children, with the creation of the Regional Regulation of Barito Kuala Regency concerning Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence.

FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL
The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb and damage psychological (psychic), physical, sexual and economic security. This is philosophically stated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire Nation and the Homeland of Indonesia.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), and is thus obligated to fulfill these provisions.

Human Rights state that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government. Through Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation.

Protection is necessary to prevent violence and physical, mental and sexual exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, and education that is appropriate to their physical and psychological development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents are obligated to understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and legal apparatus that defend the interests of children is necessary for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled on defending the best interests of the child (the best interest of the child) is necessary to realize protection that is legal in nature.

The Government of Barito Kuala Regency has established an Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) as a center for empowerment of women victims of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

From the above framework, the Government of Barito Kuala Regency is responsible for taking legal actions to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children, with the creation of the Regional Regulation of Barito Kuala Regency concerning Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence.

9. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim;
10. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions. Coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life;
11. Violence against children is any action that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom.

ELUCIDATION OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF BARITO KUALA REGENCY
NUMBER 4 OF 2015
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL
The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb and damage psychological (psychic), physical, sexual and economic security. This is philosophically stated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire Nation and the Homeland of Indonesia.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), and is thus obligated to fulfill these provisions.

Human Rights state that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government. Through Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation.

Protection is necessary to prevent violence and physical, mental and sexual exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, and education that is appropriate to their physical and psychological development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents are obligated to understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and legal apparatus that defend the interests of children is necessary for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled on defending the best interests of the child (the best interest of the child) is necessary to realize protection that is legal in nature.

The Government of Barito Kuala Regency has established an Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) as a center for empowerment of women victims of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

From the above framework, the Government of Barito Kuala Regency is responsible for taking legal actions to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children, with the creation of the Regional Regulation of Barito Kuala Regency concerning Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence.

Letter e Sufficiently clear Letter f What is meant by the right to compensation includes economic empowerment, repatriation costs, health insurance, and education or skills.
Letter g What is meant by the victim's right to rehabilitation includes: access to medical services for physical and psychological recovery, legal assistance to restore civil rights, restoration of good name, citizenship.
Letter h What is meant by the right to complaint handling is the availability of a special integrated service unit by officers.
Letter i Sufficiently clear Letter j What is meant by the right to assistance includes among others psychologists, psychiatrists, health experts, religious leaders, advocates and family members.
What is meant by assistant is an individual who works as a volunteer to provide protection and support to women and children who are victims of acts of violence during the judicial process, these assistants can come from family members, friends or independent organizations that provide attention to witnesses and victims or advocates.

Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively through information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral.
5. Task Force for Prevention and Handling of Human Trafficking Crimes, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts of human trafficking crimes in Barito Kuala Regency.
6. Woman is a person who has female genitalia who can menstruate and become pregnant or has obtained legal status as a woman.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those in the womb.
8. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, class, social status, socio-economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
9. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim;
10. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions. Coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life;
11. Violence against children is any action that results in misery or suffering to children physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom.
12. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household;
13. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited;
14. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death.
15. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
16. Economic violence is any act that deliberately neglects family members in the form of not providing a proper livelihood, care or maintenance.
17. Psychological violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person.
18. Victim is a woman and child who experiences and/or suffers either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
19. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Police, Prosecutor's Office, Courts, Social Institutions, or other parties who know or hear or violence against women has occurred.
20. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
21. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
22. Optimal service is a dynamic effort consisting of various interrelated parts, followed by performance offered by one party to another party by providing benefits, in order to achieve the best goal.
23. Information is a message (speech or expression) or collection of messages consisting of order sequences of symbols, or meanings that can be interpreted from messages or collections of messages and can be recorded or transmitted.
24. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and or mother;
25. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children and among people who are their dependents.
26. Society is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL
The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb and damage psychological (psychic), physical, sexual and economic security. This is philosophically stated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire Nation and the Homeland of Indonesia.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), and is thus obligated to fulfill these provisions.

Human Rights state that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government. Through Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation.

Protection is necessary to prevent violence and physical, mental and sexual exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, and education that is appropriate to their physical and psychological development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents are obligated to understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and legal apparatus that defend the interests of children is necessary for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled on defending the best interests of the child (the best interest of the child) is necessary to realize protection that is legal in nature.

The Government of Barito Kuala Regency has established an Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) as a center for empowerment of women victims of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

From the above framework, the Government of Barito Kuala Regency is responsible for taking legal actions to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children, with the creation of the Regional Regulation of Barito Kuala Regency concerning Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence.

I. GENERAL
The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb and damage psychological (psychic), physical, sexual and economic security. This is philosophically stated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire Nation and the Homeland of Indonesia.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), and is thus obligated to fulfill these provisions.

Human Rights state that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government. Through Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation.

Protection is necessary to prevent violence and physical, mental and sexual exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, and education that is appropriate to their physical and psychological development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents are obligated to understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and legal apparatus that defend the interests of children is necessary for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled on defending the best interests of the child (the best interest of the child) is necessary to realize protection that is legal in nature.

The Government of Barito Kuala Regency has established an Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) as a center for empowerment of women victims of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

From the above framework, the Government of Barito Kuala Regency is responsible for taking legal actions to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children, with the creation of the Regional Regulation of Barito Kuala Regency concerning Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence.

NUMBER 4 OF 2015
CONCERNING

FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL
The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb and damage psychological (psychic), physical, sexual and economic security. This is philosophically stated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire Nation and the Homeland of Indonesia.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), and is thus obligated to fulfill these provisions.

Human Rights state that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government. Through Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation.

Protection is necessary to prevent violence and physical, mental and sexual exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, and education that is appropriate to their physical and psychological development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents are obligated to understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and legal apparatus that defend the interests of children is necessary for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled on defending the best interests of the child (the best interest of the child) is necessary to realize protection that is legal in nature.

The Government of Barito Kuala Regency has established an Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) as a center for empowerment of women victims of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

From the above framework, the Government of Barito Kuala Regency is responsible for taking legal actions to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children, with the creation of the Regional Regulation of Barito Kuala Regency concerning Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence.

Article 12

Letter c What is meant by legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants or advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive.
Letter d What is meant by repatriation is returning women and children victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point or from the receiving area to the area of origin.

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and children victims of violence comprehensively through information services, assistance and legal aid, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral.

7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those in the womb.
8. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, class, social status, socio-economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that results in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
9. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim;
10. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically including threats of certain actions. Coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life;

13. 20. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
21. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
22. Optimal service is a dynamic effort consisting of various interrelated parts, followed by performance offered by one party to another party by providing benefits, in order to achieve the best goal.
23. Information is a message (speech or expression) or collection of messages consisting of order sequences of symbols, or meanings that can be interpreted from messages or collections of messages and can be recorded or transmitted.
24. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and or mother;
25. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, and mother and her children and among people who are their dependents.
26. Society is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.

Article 26
(1) Regional governments may provide financial assistance to community organizations, social organizations or non-governmental organizations that implement protection of women and children from discrimination and acts of violence.
(2) Financial assistance as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be in accordance with regional financial capacity, and implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the field of regional finance.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF BARITO KUALA REGENCY
NUMBER 4 OF 2015
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL
The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb and damage psychological (psychic), physical, sexual and economic security. This is philosophically stated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire Nation and the Homeland of Indonesia.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), and is thus obligated to fulfill these provisions.

Human Rights state that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government. Through Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation.

Protection is necessary to prevent violence and physical, mental and sexual exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, and education that is appropriate to their physical and psychological development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents are obligated to understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and legal apparatus that defend the interests of children is necessary for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled on defending the best interests of the child (the best interest of the child) is necessary to realize protection that is legal in nature.

The Government of Barito Kuala Regency has established an Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) as a center for empowerment of women victims of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

From the above framework, the Government of Barito Kuala Regency is responsible for taking legal actions to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children, with the creation of the Regional Regulation of Barito Kuala Regency concerning Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence.

What is meant by social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

I. GENERAL
The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb and damage psychological (psychic), physical, sexual and economic security. This is philosophically stated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution, that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia is to protect the entire Nation and the Homeland of Indonesia.

Therefore, the Government of Indonesia has signed the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR 1948) and ratified CEDAW (Law Number 7 of 1984 concerning the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women), and is thus obligated to fulfill these provisions.

Human Rights state that the enforcement and fulfillment of Human Rights is the responsibility of the State, especially the Government. Through Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, the Government recognizes the existence of children's rights. The inherent rights of children include basic rights as human beings, namely the Right to Life, the Right to Growth and Development, the Right to Protection and the Right to Participation.

Protection is necessary to prevent violence and physical, mental and sexual exploitation. To fulfill the right to growth and development, children need space to play, exercise, and education that is appropriate to their physical and psychological development. In fulfilling children's rights, every government administrator, community and parents are obligated to understand and care about children's rights. The existence of legal instruments and legal apparatus that defend the interests of children is necessary for this protection effort. Legislation that is principled on defending the best interests of the child (the best interest of the child) is necessary to realize protection that is legal in nature.

The Government of Barito Kuala Regency has established an Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A) as a center for empowerment of women victims of violence which specifically has the main duties and functions for empowerment of women and children victims of violence.

From the above framework, the Government of Barito Kuala Regency is responsible for taking legal actions to prevent, suppress, reduce, and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children, with the creation of the Regional Regulation of Barito Kuala Regency concerning Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence.

Letter a What is meant by trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by means of the threat of force, use of force, abduction, confinement, forgery of documents or identity, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over that person or another person, whether carried out within the country or between countries for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
Letter b What is meant by exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim which includes prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical sexual reproductive organs or unlawfully, transferring/utilizing power or transplanting organs and or body tissues or utilizing the power or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
Letter c Sufficiently clear Letter d What is meant by witness is a person who sees, hears and experiences events of violence and human rights violations.
Letter e Mediation is carried out for cases of domestic violence that fall into the category of complaint offenses as regulated in Law No. 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence.
